name: Conditional Access Policy Weakened 'For Testing'
description: An IT admin disables the 'require compliant device for all users' Conditional Access policy at 14:02 to debug a partner integration. They forget. Six hours later attackers spray credentials from non-corporate devices and walk straight into Exchange.
reasoning: Identity edge + downstream M365 services. The simulation shows the policy flip (low-volume admin event), then a delayed attack timing that maps to attackers waking up in their tz, then containment.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline; CA policy 'require compliant device' enabled and enforcing.
14:02 UTC — admin disables the policy 'temporarily' and forgets to restore.
Spray begins from 50+ residential IPs (botnet); 0.5% of attempts succeed (re-used passwords).
Successful logins from non-managed devices to Exchange Web Services for ~14 accounts.
Mailbox forwarding rules added on 6 of those accounts (BEC pattern).
UEBA + DLP correlate 'no compliant device' + 'new forwarding rule'. SOC paged.
CA policy re-enabled; affected sessions revoked; forwarding rules removed.
Steady state. New rule: any disable of tier-0 CA policy auto-restores after 60 minutes.
